dedupe_keys.name: niosh firefighter body dimensions for fire apparatus and protective equipment design 71 measurements

description: This dataset gives body dimensions of US firefighters measured to update ergonomic and safety specifications for fire apparatus and protective equipment. It was produced by the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health, part of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and the page was archived in 2025 on DataLumos, the ICPSR repository for federal data. It presents 71 measurements relevant to seats, seat belts, cabs, turnout gear, gloves and head and face equipment: 40 taken in fitted shorts in standing and seated postures, 21 taken while firefighters wore their own turnout gear with the tools they carry in their pockets, and 10 hand, head and face dimensions extracted from three-dimensional scans. The producer describes it as the first national anthropometric information on US firefighters. The archived files are free to download from DataLumos after sign-in; as a federal work it carries no copyright restrictions, although the archive record states no licence. Caveats: the measurements date from the original NIOSH study, and sample details must be read from the archived documentation. Simulation uses: occupant dimensions for fire apparatus cab and equipment design checks. Related records: the NFPA fire department profile tables (data-nfpa-us-fire-department-profile-supporting-tables) give the workforce size, and the NFPA fatality reports (data-nfpa-fatal-firefighter-injuries-united-states) cover injuries.
